A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the emotional and suicidal problems experienced by Nigerian children with chronic physical illnesses are significant, and these problems are more prevalent in children with JDM than SCD, and in the mothers of children with chronic illness.

there exists a high burden of emotional disorders among children with chronic physical illnesses in this environment, and this burden is higher among children who suffer chronic physical illness and their mothers when compared with healthy children and their mothers, and there is need for development of pediatric liaison services in pediatric clinics to address this burden.
the psychological distress of children with chronic illness in this setting is not just a reflection of their physical condition, but also of their mothers’ distress.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there is a need to develop liaison services in pediatric clinics in Nigeria and other sub – Saharan African countries that would provide psychological interventions for children with chronic medical illness and their families.

there is need to develop and strengthen pediatric liaison services in Nigeria and other sub-Saharan African countries in order to address the emotional and psychological problems of children who suffer chronic physical illness and their families.

pediatricians in developing countries should be aware that psychological problems may complicate chronic physical health conditions among their patients, and should be prepared to refer these patients for psychiatric care.
